qr.ready: All set: the address, the IBAN and the currency are in order.

qrr.title: QR reference (QRR)
qrr.body: A 27-digit reference that belongs to your QR-IBAN. Your bank reports it back when the payment arrives. That is how TILL matches the payment to this invoice.

scor.title: Creditor Reference (SCOR)
scor.body: The international reference under ISO 11649, for an ordinary IBAN. It starts with RF and carries a check digit, so a typo shows up.

qr.graphicDense: This code is dense. At print size its modules fall below the 0.4 mm the guideline asks for. If a scan fails, shorten the additional information.
qr.graphicUndrawable: The payment data is too long for a Swiss QR Code. Shorten the address or the additional information.

currency.otherHint: Three letters per ISO 4217, for example USD.

qr.qrr: The payment part is created at issue, with a QR reference.
qr.scor: The payment part is created at issue, with a SCOR reference.
qr.noIban: Without a stored IBAN there is no payment part in any currency.
qr.unsupported: The QR payment part allows CHF and EUR only. You can invoice and post in {currency}, it simply gets no payment part.
qr.chfOnly: From {date} a QR-IBAN carries CHF only, so an invoice in {currency} dated on or after that gets no payment part.
qr.chfOnlyRemedy: A plain IBAN would still get you a payment part, with a SCOR reference instead. That is our inference: SIX says nothing about a creditor who holds only a QR-IBAN.
qr.chfOnlyValidity: Invoices you issue before then stay payable. Version 2.3 remains valid until November 2027.

fx.title: Conversion
fx.base: {currency} is your ledger currency. TILL converts nothing here and stores no rate.
fx.loading: TILL is looking up the rate.
fx.willPost: When you issue it, TILL posts this invoice in {baseCurrency} at this rate. The converted amounts then sit on the entry.
fx.postedNote: This is how the document sits in the books. TILL converted it at this rate when it was issued, and a rate recorded later does not change that.
fx.vatNote: The {baseCurrency} VAT is the figure your Swiss VAT return is filed on. TILL reads it off the posting instead of multiplying the rate out: the posting rounds once on the side total, so an amount times a rate lands a Rappen off often enough to matter.
fx.needsRateNoPosting: There is no admissible rate for {currency} on {date}. You can still issue this document, which posts nothing. The invoice it becomes will need the rate.
fx.needsRateEmpty: No rate has been recorded for this workspace yet.
fx.needsRateNone: There are rates for {currency}, but none covers this date.
fx.needsRateStale: The newest rate is dated {date} and is therefore older than {days} days.
fx.methodNotElected: The rate for {currency} is on the {method} basis. For tax period {taxPeriod} you are on {electedMethod}.
fx.methodLocked: The basis for {taxPeriod} is settled, a foreign-currency entry is already posted. You can switch from {period} onward.
fx.methodFix: Record the rate on the {method} basis.
fx.denied: You lack the permission to read rates.
fx.error: The rate could not be loaded.

Documents.title: Documents
Documents.body:
Every document in one list: quotes, orders, invoices and credit notes, filterable by kind and status. From here you start a new document.

A draft can be deleted. An issued document is immutable and is cancelled with a visible reversal when needed.

If you account on agreed consideration, VAT is owed on issuing the invoice, not on receipt of payment.
